spec: Remove duplicate email addresses from a list. Email comparison should be case-insensitive.

inputs.note: Typical case: mixed case duplicates across different domains and a unique entry.
Edge case: empty list should return an empty list.
Edge case: single uppercase email with no case variations.
Edge case: multiple duplicates of the exact same string in varying cases.
Edge case: repeated pattern of two alternating cases.
Edge case: emails with dots and subdomains/prefixes.
Edge case: emails with plus addressing (sub-addressing).
Edge case: trailing whitespace in one duplicate. Note: strict comparison usually keeps these separate, but testers check if trim is expected.
Edge case: exact string duplicates (no case difference).
Edge case: mix of distinct and duplicate emails.
Edge case: short TLDs and case variations.
Edge case: all four common case variations present.

def remove_duplicate_emails(emails: list[str]) -> list[str]:
    """
    emails: A list of email address strings, potentially containing duplicates with varying case.
    returns: A new list with duplicates removed. Comparison is case-insensitive.
             The relative order of first occurrences is preserved.
    """
    seen: set[str] = set()
    result: list[str] = []
    for email in emails:
        lowered = email.lower()
        if lowered not in seen:
            seen.add(lowered)
            result.append(email)
    return result

questions.text: Should only the domain part of an email be compared case‑insensitively, while the local part remains case‑sensitive?
questions.why: The current code lower‑cases the entire address, so "User@example.com" and "user@example.com" are treated as duplicates; a domain‑only rule would keep both.

options.label: Whole address lower‑cased for duplicate detection
Only domain lower‑cased, local part case‑sensitive

questions.text: Should leading or trailing whitespace be ignored when deciding if two emails are duplicates?
questions.why: The implementation treats "user@domain.com" and "user@domain.com " as distinct, preserving both; trimming would collapse them into one.

options.label: Whitespace is significant; no trimming performed

questions.text: Should empty strings be considered valid email entries and kept in the result?
questions.why: The current behavior retains an empty string as a unique entry; filtering them out would drop the empty value from the output.

options.label: Empty strings are kept like any other value
Discard empty strings before duplicate removal
